title: Check-Up
concept: A short, honest count to tell needing space apart from pulling away, so you know which repair to reach for. One sheet, three lenses: drifting apart, pulling away, and gaps between what you say and what you do. It describes behaviour you can both see, never your partner’s intent. About every few months, 20 minutes.
whenToUse: When dinner is all logistics, replies have an edge, one of you is carrying the work, or the last real question was weeks ago. Also sooner if resentment is building or “we’re fine” sits beside loneliness.
steps: Safety first. Fear or coercion: stop and get outside support. Steady contempt (sneering, mocking, belittling) is also a serious sign: a Check-Up won’t fix it, so talk to a professional. Never use the signs to question where your partner goes, who they see or what they plan. A partner who has stopped sharing because they are afraid is not pulling away: use the Help Lines.
Each of you marks, on your own, what you’ve noticed on the one sheet, using the three lenses under Practise. Describe behaviour you’ve seen; don’t claim to know the other’s intent.
Compare only if you both want to. Either of you may decline to compare counts.

Read the result. No signs: keep up the Daily Rhythm. One or two: you likely need some space and a few small repairs (Micro-Repair, Daily Rhythm). Three or more: bring back the Daily Rhythm for two weeks.

Pick one pattern or gap and one fix for 14 days, then look again. If nothing has shifted, agree a Full Repair date if you both want to; either of you may say no. A specific breach of trust goes to Trust Recovery.

phrases.text: I’m noticing some distance. Do you need space, or is it something bigger?
I’m carrying most of the load. Can we share it out, specifically?
Can we put a date on this instead of hoping?

working: A ticks three signs and B ticks four. Both tick the same three: less curiosity, mostly practical talk, repairs that feel routine. They bring back the Daily Rhythm for two weeks, then look again. Nothing has shifted, so they both agree to book a Full Repair.
notWorking: The weekends have gone quiet, and A decides to say nothing and wait for B to notice. A month goes by with nothing booked, and the quiet starts to feel normal.
activity: Lens 1, drifting apart. Score each from 0 to 2 for the past month: drifting into housemates (polite but lonely); the tone souring (replies with an edge); one of you carrying the work; waiting for later (“it’ll be better after…”). Fixes: Daily Rhythm; Micro-Repair now and soften your tone a little first; share the load out at the monthly part of your Weekly Reset. Lens 2, pulling away. The eight signs: (1) fewer non-logistical hellos, (2) less curiosity about each other, (3) avoiding future plans, (4) doing more on your own in place of shared time (time apart is healthy), (5) mostly practical talk, (6) going-through-the-motions affection, (7) repairs that feel routine, (8) contempt instead of frustration. Lens 3, say-and-do gaps. Set what you agreed to do against what happened on an ordinary week. Each names one gap, picks one small correction to their own behaviour, and owns the small part of the other’s concern that is true. Share only what you choose to; your own notes are never owed. Turn a shared gap into one small agreed change. For a friction that keeps coming back, find the closest match in Appendix A and choose where to step in.
warn: Contempt, fear or coercion at any count: stop; safety and outside support come first. Never use the signs to question where your partner goes, who they see or what they plan. This starts a conversation. It is not a verdict or a score to hold against anyone, and wanting time alone or plans of your own isn’t a sign by itself.
note: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this tool, not a failure of it.
